newsitem.title: USA: U.S corp debt issues on hold ahead of FOMC meeting.
newsitem.headline: U.S corp debt issues on hold ahead of FOMC meeting.

text.p: Corporate bond primary sector activity is expected to remain on hold as U.S. Federal Reserve policy-makers get set to meet on Tuesday, players said.
"Today and tomorrow will be very quiet," said one high-grade syndicate source. "No one is going to do anything ahead of this meeting."
On Tuesday, the Fed's policy-setting arm, the Federal Open Market Committee, will meet to vote on U.S. monetary policy.
Results of a preliminary Reuter poll show that U.S. experts are equally divided over whether the Fed will maintain policy as it stands or hike rates by 25 basis points.

While a positive change in market sentiment could lure some players back into the new issue arena after the FOMC meeting, the likelihood of that is not expected to be great during a shortened holiday week, high-grade syndicate sources said.
"We're going to see little to nothing this week," said another investment-grade syndicate source. "No one wants to be lugging anything around ahead of the FOMC and a shortened week."
The market will see an early close on Friday ahead of next Monday's U.S. Memorial Day holiday when markets will close.
The bulk of this week's new issue activity is seen coming from the private placement market where a number of deals are slated for mid-week pricings, high-yield syndicate sources said.
Several deals totalling about $1.0 billion are expected to hit the corporate bond primary sector this week, they said.
Integrated Health Services Inc is slated to bring $250 million in 10-year 144A senior subordinated notes via Salomon Brothers, sources said.
Wells Aluminum Corp, a Baltimore, Maryland-based manufacturer of aluminum extrusion and fabricated products, is expected to sell $100 million in 144A eight-year senior notes via Merrill Lynch.
Another $100 million in five-year 144A notes is expected from Navistar Financial Corp via JP Morgan Securities.
Energy Corp of America will bring $150 million in 10-year 144A senior subordinated notes via Chase Securities.
DGS INternational Finance Co BV is also expected to bring a US$150 10-year 144A guaranteed notes via BT Securities.
Also, Compania Lationomericana De Infraestructura Servicios (CLISA) is expected to issue $100 million in senior seven-year 144A guaranteed notes via Citicorp Securities.
Among other high-yield offerings, Chief Auto Parts Inc, an auto parts retailer, is slated to bring $125 million eight-year senior notes via CS First Boston.
Looking ahead, in the high-grade sector, a few deals have emerged for next week's business, players said.
Hartford Insurance is expected to sell $600 million in a three-part debt offering consisting of seven-year, 10-year and 30-year maturities, dealers said.
Also, Frontier Corp, a telephone long distance carrier, is expected to set $300 million in A3/A rated seven-year debt via Salomon Brothers.

Briggs & Stratton Corp, a maker of engines for lawn and garden equipment, is expected to bring $100 million in 10-year debt and $75 million in five-year debt via Credit Suisse First Boston, sources said.
In the government market, the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was up 1/32 at 96-16/32 to yield 6.90 percent.
